gaps.quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
gaps.note: Does not follow from the preceding sentence, which only requires q not to divide each denominator xi, and as stated it is false for zero entries (q divides 0). The page never says how the odd prime q is chosen. The paper (Lemma lem:matrix-shear, lines 1394-1420) chooses an odd prime avoiding every denominator in the finite table of factors and inverses and every numerator of a diagonal entry of an invertible factor (for example a prime exceeding all nonzero numerators and denominators), so that the triangular factors stay invertible mod q^b.

gaps.quote: where $F_1$ and $F_2$ are lower-triangular rational matrices
gaps.note: Missing hypothesis: the paper's Lemma lem:lower-lower (line 1370) requires E_1, E_2 to be invertible lower-triangular matrices. The page later uses F_1^{-1} and F_2^{-1}, which need this; as written (any lower-triangular matrices) the factorization claim does not support those steps.

Stated about every partial permutation matrix, which is false: a partial permutation matrix can have any number of ones. Only the Pi produced by the factorization of M has exactly rank M ones (paper line 1370-1372, Pi has exactly a entries equal to one). Also the page does not argue why elimination ends with exactly rank-many ones.

gaps.term: tape order needed for the additions
gaps.quote: So the shear needs $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}M$ interchanges plus $O(V)$ further work.
gaps.note: The O(V) cost of the additions D_tau <- D_tau + H_sigma rests on a hypothesis the page never states: in the paper (lines 1396-1410, 1448-1452) every H_i lies before every D_j on tape, so the first and last updates target a later field controlled by an earlier field and run in linear time via the ordered-affine-streams lemma. The page does not say the fields are in tape order, and gives no cost argument for these two additions.

gaps.quote: Update coordinates from last to first, so each becomes a fixed combination of earlier, still unchanged, coordinates.
gaps.note: Linear time needs the coordinates to be stored in order on the tape so that earlier fields can be streamed while a later field is updated (paper lines 1425-1431, using Lemma ordered-affine-streams, descending physical order). The page does not state this layout assumption or what the cited cost result says about the machine; it also needs the diagonal entries to be units mod q^b, which the page's q-condition (see above) only covers if corrected.

gaps.quote: The network's rank budget, which counts dimension changes along its edges, gives $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}R-N+2L_{\rm b}$
gaps.note: The formula is presented without derivation or citation, and the reader is not told what the bit network's edges, 'negative source projections' or 'decreasing edges' are, so N and L_b cannot be interpreted or checked. The page also says each edge 'carries such a matrix', while in the paper (lines 1142-1166, 1458-1466) matrices sit on gates and terminals and the edge matrix is the difference M_head - M_tail; the rank of that difference equals the dimension change except for the N source edges.

gaps.quote: Per wire, the interchanges are fewer than $R$, which the recurrence turns into a saving of a power of the chunk width (the chunk length).
gaps.note: No recurrence is given, and 'chunk width' is not defined. s_b < W_b R only says the average per wire is below R; a saving of a power needs a quantitative bound. The paper (lines 1321-1342) uses the explicit relative deficit eta_b = 339/22587335000000 > 20*2^-50 to obtain s_b/W_b < m^tau with tau = 1-2^-50. 'Fewer than R' alone does not yield that.
